title: Transient session data protocol — workshop notes and DPA addendum sketch
content:
Summary:

Notes from the 2025-11-18 customer workshop focused on handling transient session payloads for a sensitive POC. The customer (healthtech pilot) requires minimal retention of raw user prompts and wants a verifiable deletion pathway for both hosted and dedicated deployments. This doc captures the proposed protocol, a light DPA addendum sketch, engineering constraints, and an action list for follow-ups.

Attendees:
- Sofia Martinez (SE, owner)
- Liam O'Connor (SE)
- Priya Desai (Solutions Architect)
- Marco Alvarez (Customer Success)
- Jenna Brooks (Legal)
- Akira Tanaka (SRE)
- Customer reps: S. Gupta (Data Privacy Lead), M. Li (Platform)

Context and ask:
- Customer POC uses Redwood Hosted API for ingestion and real-time chat.
- They must ensure: (1) raw prompt text is ephemeral by default; (2) any retained material is encrypted and accessible only to customer; (3) clear audit trail for deletion requests; (4) minimal telemetry shared with Redwood support.
- POC target: 6-week pilot, optional Dedicated runway.

High-level protocol (proposal):
1) Session-first ephemeral mode (default).
   - All session-level user input stored in an in-memory KV cache per session, never written to persistent blob store unless explicitly checkpointed.
   - TTL: in-memory only until session termination + 30s grace to flush to ephemeral logs. No long-term storage.

2) Checkpointing opt-in (customer-side flag).
   - If the customer sets checkpoint=true in request metadata, agent will persist a minimal record: hashed prompt (SHA-256), model-version, timestamp, result-id. Raw prompt stored only if customer-provided "store_raw=true" and accepted by contract.

3) Pseudonymized analytics stream.
   - Aggregated metrics (token counts, latency percentiles) are shipped to Redwood internal telemetry. No raw text. Any identifiers are salted and hashed using customer-specific salt.

4) On-demand deletion API and cross-system GC.
   - Provide a /session-delete endpoint that accepts session_id or result_id and triggers immediate: (a) delete from persistent store, (b) invalidate cache, (c) emit deletion event to audit log, (d) mark in index as deleted.
   - Downstream propagation: S3 lifecycle rules, Kafka retention reset, and DB tombstone write. Most propagation windows: 0-5 minutes for primary stores, 1-24 hours for analytics pipelines requiring re-index.

Retention matrix (proposed POC defaults):
- Ephemeral session buffers: 0 days (in-memory) + 30s flush grace
- Persistent transcripts (opt-in): 7 days (default) configurable to 0 / 30 / 90
- Aggregated usage metrics: 90 days
- Error logs (no user text): 30 days
- Backups: 14 days snapshot retention encrypted with CMK

Redaction & scrubbing patterns:
- Apply regex-based scrubbing pipeline on any persisted text: PII detectors -> replace with [REDACTED_TYPE] token. For health PII, run domain-specific patterns.
- Two-tier approach: quick-scrub (regex) for near-line writes, deep-scrub (ML-based PII model) during background job before analytics share.

Encryption and key control:
- Hosted: server-side encryption with customer-managed key (CMK) option.
- Dedicated/Private: recommended to use customer KMS (Bring-Your-Own-Key) and restrict Redwood operator key access.

Auditability and evidence for deletion:
- Deletion event log contains: requestor identity, session/result id, timestamp, store ids, and final confirmation code. Logs are retained for 365 days (metadata only, no raw text).
- Provide a signed deletion certificate (JSON with HMAC) to customer once deletion completes.

DPA addendum sketch (language to iterate with Legal):
Addendum: Transient Session Data
1. Definitions: "Transient Session Data" means unpersisted or in-memory inputs submitted by Data Subjects that are not checkpointed to long-term storage.
2. Storage: Provider will retain Transient Session Data only in volatile memory during the session and for no longer than 30 seconds after session termination unless Customer expressly opts to persist data via checkpointing controls.
3. Deletion and Certification: Upon Customer request, Provider will delete persisted records associated with provided session IDs and will issue a signed deletion certificate within 24 hours. Metadata evidencing the deletion (e.g., tombstone ID, timestamp) may be retained for up to 365 days solely for compliance and audit purposes.
4. Key Management: For persisted data, Provider will support Customer-managed encryption keys (CMK) and document the key rotation policy in the deployment runbook.

Operational notes and constraints:
- Host-level snapshots: Need to ensure ephemeral buffers are excluded from nightly snapshots. Action: infra to add exclude pattern for ephemeral mount paths. Owner: Akira.
- Analytics reprocessing may rehydrate derived tokens from persisted checkpoints. Mitigation: apply strict PII redaction before analytic ingestion. Owner: Priya.
- Deletion propagation edge cases: cached search indexes and third-party backups. We need a TTL + reindex flow. Action: design a 'retract and reindex' job for Elastic indices. Owner: Liam.

Customer-specific variances discussed:
- Customer will likely require: (a) CMK with HSM-backed keys, (b) restricted Redwood support access, (c) SAML-based admin delete requests only.
- They asked for SLA: deletion acknowledgement within 24 hours and full propagation within 72 hours. We tentatively accept for POC, escalate for contract if Dedicated.

Open questions for Legal/Privacy:
- Is storing hashed prompt (SHA-256) considered personal data under GDPR if the prompt contains PII? Jenna: likely yes if reversible via rainbow tables; recommend keyed-hash (HMAC) with customer salt and KDF.
- Are deletion certificates sufficient evidence for regulated auditors? Jenna: acceptable as long as logs show chain-of-custody; may require notarized workflow for high-regulated verticals.
- Data subject access requests (DSAR): mapping between session/result ids and subject may require additional PII linkage. Need to define scope of retrieval.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- [Sofia] Draft DPA addendum language updated with HMAC phrasing and sample certificate payload. ETA: 2025-11-25.
- [Jenna] Legal review of deletion certificate acceptability and recommended metadata retention window. ETA: 2025-11-30.
- [Akira] Infra: confirm snapshot exclusion and implement ephemeral mount exclusion. ETA: 2025-12-04.
- [Liam] Create Elastic reindex prototype and document retraction job. ETA: 2025-12-08.
- [Priya] PII deep-scrub pipeline prototype and test dataset for health domain. ETA: 2025-12-11.
- [Marco] Update POC runbook and customer-facing one-pager describing the transient protocol and deletion guarantee. ETA: 2025-11-27.

Decision log:
- 2025-11-18: Default for POC will be ephemeral session buffers with opt-in checkpointing.
- 2025-11-18: Hashes for analytics will use HMAC with customer-provided salt where feasible.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Analytics processing may inadvertently expose derived sensitive signals. Mitigation: enforce ML-based PII detection before any analytic share, quarantine flagged records.
- Risk: Third-party backup retention. Mitigation: review backup policies and mark POC buckets as non-archival.

Next steps with customer:
- Run a short checklist demo showing: (1) session creation without persistence, (2) opt-in checkpoint flow, (3) call to /session-delete and receipt of deletion certificate. Schedule for week of 2025-11-24.
- Follow-up meeting to agree SLA metrics for deletion propagation and to sign a light DPA addendum for the pilot.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep sample deletion certificate small: {session_id, deleted_stores:[..], ts, signature}. Consider JWT or signed JSON.
- For POC, prefer implementation patterns that can later be toggled by flag rather than hard-coded branches so Dedicated migrations are easier.

References and places to update after this workshop:
- Confluence page: Transient Session Data (linked above)
- Runbook template: SE-poc-template/runbooks/transient-data.md
- Github prototype: github.com/redwood-inference/poc-scripts (PR #12)

End of notes.
